title: PhishGuard
narration: This is PhishGuard, an AI-based phishing website detection and risk analysis system by Ayushi Tiwari, guided by Mister Vishal Gupta.
caption: Ayushi Tiwari · Guide: Mr. Vishal Gupta · Lloyd Institute of Engineering & Technology

actions.heading: PhishGuard
actions.sub:
AI-Based Phishing Website Detection and Risk Analysis System Using Machine Learning
B.Tech Mini Project · Ayushi Tiwari · Guide: Mr. Vishal Gupta
Lloyd Institute of Engineering & Technology · AKTU

title: The problem
narration: Phishing sites copy trusted brands to steal passwords, and many vanish before blocklists catch them. PhishGuard explains the risk of any link.
caption: Phishing pages copy trusted brands and vanish fast; blocklists alone react too late

actions.heading: The problem
actions.sub:
Phishing websites imitate trusted brands to steal passwords and card details.
Many live only for hours, so blocklists alone react too late.
Users need an instant, explainable risk check for any link.

title: How it works
narration: Each URL becomes forty-four features for a Random Forest model, while live checks inspect DNS, who-is, SSL, content, brands and threat feeds.
caption: URL → 44 features → Random Forest + live checks → 60% ML + 40% heuristics → risk 0–100

actions.heading: How PhishGuard works
actions.sub:
URL → validation → 44 lexical features → Random Forest ML model
+ live checks: DNS · WHOIS · SSL · HTTP & content · brand · threat feeds
Risk score 0–100 = 60% ML + 40% heuristics (blocklist hit ≥ 90)
→ verdict, trust score & tier, explained report

title: Overview dashboard
narration: The Overview dashboard shows total scans, detection rate and average trust score, with trends and a live scan feed.
caption: KPIs, scan trends, verdict split and a live feed that refreshes every 5 seconds

title: Deep scan a suspicious URL
narration: Let's deep scan a fake PayPal login link. Eight stages run, from the ML prediction to DNS, who-is, SSL and reputation.
caption: Scanning http://paypal-login-verify.secure-account.xyz/update with an 8-stage deep scan

actions.text: Deep scan (DNS, WHOIS, SSL, HTTP, screenshot)

note: Deep scan is ON by default (no toggle click). The scan takes about 3 s; the app then auto-navigates to /scans/<new id> (450 ms delay). Dry run of the real pipeline on a scratch DB copy gave: phishing, risk 92, trust 8, tier Untrusted, social_engineering, PayPal via subdomain.

title: Verdict: phishing
narration: The verdict is phishing: risk ninety-two out of a hundred, trust score eight, tier Untrusted, threat type social engineering.
caption: Risk 92/100 · Trust score 8/100 · Tier: Untrusted · Social engineering · ML 98.5%
note: :latest = the scan created in scene 'scan': take the id from the current URL (/scans/<id>) after the Scan page auto-navigates; fallback = newest scan whose url is http://paypal-login-verify.secure-account.xyz/update. Do NOT use the newest scan id: the watchlist scheduler creates scans in the background. Do not reload if the path already matches. If expect.risk_score differs, update the spoken numbers (trust = 100 - risk) and the caption.

title: Explainable result
narration: Every verdict is explained: an AI summary, the factors behind it, and a sixty-forty split between model and checks.
caption: AI summary, negative and positive factors, and the 60% ML + 40% heuristics score breakdown

title: ML Explanation & Brand
narration: ML Explanation shows the features behind the prediction, like the long hostname, and all four models agree. Brand confirms PayPal impersonation.
caption: Feature contributions, all 4 models agree (95–100%), PayPal impersonated via subdomain
note: Per-model probabilities from the dry run: Logistic Regression 100%, Decision Tree 100%, Random Forest 98.5%, SVM 95.3%. Top contribution: Hostname length.

title: Live checks on a real phishing kit
narration: Next, a live phishing kit on vercel dot app: who-is and DNS records, a mismatched SSL certificate, and its redirect chain.
caption: Live kit on vercel.app: WHOIS & DNS, SSL hostname mismatch, redirect chain & headers
note: :phishing = newest scan of http://www.indesx-mauve.vercel.app/, which is also the first item of GET /api/scans?verdict=phishing&sort=risk_score&order=desc (risk 97). The watchlist re-checks this URL, so the id changes (#70, #71, ...); all of them show the same facts. Narration in this scene and the next two is specific to this site.

title: Reputation & content
narration: Reputation shows three of eleven engines flagging it, including OpenPhish and Phishing Army. Content classifies it as a login page.
caption: 3 of 11 engines flag it (OpenPhish, Phishing Army, PhishGuard ML) · category: login

title: Resources, source & graph
narration: Resources lists contacted domains, Source keeps the HTML, which hides code sending stolen data to Telegram, and Graph maps the infrastructure.
caption: Contacted domains, stored HTML (Telegram exfiltration code) and the infrastructure graph

actions.selector: Search the page source (Enter = next, Shift+Enter = previous)

note: Scope tab clicks to [data-report-tabs]: 'Graph' is also a sidebar link and 'Source' is a substring of 'Resources'. Stored HTML of scan #70 contains 'telegram' twice.

title: A legitimate site: github.com
narration: For contrast, github dot com is legitimate: risk three, trust score ninety-seven, tier Trusted, and no engine flags it.
caption: github.com: legitimate · risk 3/100 · trust score 97/100 · Tier: Trusted · 0/11 engines
note: :legit = newest scan whose URL is https://github.com (currently #69).

title: History & bulk scanning
narration: History keeps every scan with export and one-click pivots, like all Untrusted sites. Bulk Scan checks up to five hundred URLs.
caption: Pivot by tier, threat type, IP, ASN or registrar · CSV/JSON export · bulk jobs of 500 URLs
note: The first 'Untrusted' on the page is the active filter chip. Bulk: type only, do not submit.

title: Analytics
narration: Analytics shows scan trends, an activity heatmap, threat types, trust tiers and a detection funnel from scanned to phishing.
caption: Scan trends, weekday × hour heatmap, threat types, trust tiers and the detection funnel

title: Model Lab: why Random Forest
narration: The Model Lab compares four classifiers on one hundred forty-six thousand URLs. Random Forest wins on F1, with eighty-six percent accuracy even on unseen domains, and an A U C of zero point nine four.
caption: 146,364 URLs · 4 models · Random Forest: accuracy 86.4%, F1 0.856, ROC-AUC 0.945
note: metrics.json: 146,364 URLs (73,241 phishing / 73,123 legit), 44 features. Random Forest test: accuracy 0.8638, precision 0.908, recall 0.8098, F1 0.8561, ROC-AUC 0.9449 (LR F1 0.8045, DT 0.8372, SVM 0.8329). Realistic set of 4,000 unseen-domain URLs: RF accuracy 0.864, AUC 0.9421.

title: Graph, Watchlist & Typosquat
narration: The Relationship graph links domains by shared IP addresses and registrars. Watchlist re-checks sites automatically, and Typosquat finds live PayPal look-alikes.
caption: Infrastructure graph, scheduled re-checks with alerts, and live look-alikes of paypal.com
note: /typosquat?domain=paypal.com runs about 60 live DNS checks on load and can take several seconds; consider pre-warming it once before recording.

title: Community & threat feeds
narration: Community reports work like PhishTank, with crowd voting, and Threat Feeds holds six hundred fifty-seven thousand blocklist entries.
caption: PhishTank-style voting (verified at +3 net votes) · 657,124 entries from 5 blocklists
note: 657,124 = GET /api/health feeds_entries (OpenPhish, URLhaus, Phishing.Database, PhishTank, Phishing Army).

title: Alerts, activity log & settings
narration: Alerts flag high-risk detections, the Activity log records every action, Settings tunes the thresholds, and a REST API exposes everything.
caption: Alerts, a full audit trail, adjustable verdict thresholds and a documented REST API

title: Architecture
narration: Under the hood: a React dashboard, a Fast API backend with the model and analysis engine, and S Q Lite storage, on Vercel.
caption: React dashboard → FastAPI → ML model + analysis engine → SQLite · deployed on Vercel

actions.heading: Architecture
actions.sub:
React 19 + Vite + Tailwind + Recharts dashboard
→ FastAPI REST backend (Python)
→ scikit-learn Random Forest + analysis engine (DNS, WHOIS/RDAP, SSL, HTTP, brand, feeds)
→ SQLite database · deployed on Vercel
